concepts.title: Column Maximum and Minimum Marks
concepts.definition: DataFrame.max() and DataFrame.min() reduce each column to its largest and smallest entry, and their difference measures the spread of the column. A column of exam scores, for instance the set 92, 95, 85, 80, 75, 50 from the chapter's activity, shrinks to just three numbers: the top score, the bottom score and the gap between them.
concepts.key_idea: Highest entry minus lowest entry gives the spread; both extremes come straight from max() and min() without sorting.
question_patterns: find the maximum and minimum of the scores 92, 95, 85, 80, 75 and 50
compute the range of the marks column using max() and min()
which parameter of max() restricts the output to numeric columns only
what does df.max(axis=1) return for the marksUT DataFrame
find the minimum marks obtained by Mishti in each subject across the unit tests
the top score is 95 and the lowest is 50; what is the score range

solution_steps.explain: max() over the six scores returns 95
solution_steps.compute: score_max = max((s_one, s_two, s_three, s_four, s_five, s_six))

solution_steps.explain: min() over the same six scores returns 50
solution_steps.compute: score_min = min((s_one, s_two, s_three, s_four, s_five, s_six))

solution_steps.explain: 95 - 50 = 45 is the spread of the scores

worked_examples.q: Scores are 92, 95, 85, 80, 75, 50. What is the column maximum?

concepts.title: Column Sum and Mean of Marks
concepts.definition: DataFrame.sum() adds a numeric column end to end and DataFrame.mean() divides that total by the number of entries. For the twelve Maths marks of the marksUT DataFrame the total is 231 and the mean works out to 19.25, matching the count, mean rows of describe().
concepts.key_idea: Add the column once, divide once by the value count; the sum feeds the mean directly.
question_patterns: find the total of the Maths column of the marksUT DataFrame
compute the mean of the twelve Maths marks 22, 21, 14, 20, 23, 22, 23, 24, 12, 15, 18, 17

verify that the sum of the Maths marks divided by twelve gives 19.25
write the statement that prints only the total of the Maths column

solution_steps.explain: 231 / 12 = 19.25, the mean reported by describe()

worked_examples.q: Twelve Maths marks total 231. What is their mean?

concepts.title: Raman Row Sum Percentage
concepts.definition: A row-wise sum with axis=1 adds one student's marks across all subjects of one unit test. Raman's Unit Test 1 row 22, 21, 18, 20, 21 totals 102, and expressing it against the maximum possible 25 times 5 subjects turns the total into a percentage.
concepts.key_idea: Sum across the row with axis=1, then scale by 100 against the ceiling of 25 marks per subject.

express Raman's Unit Test 1 total of 102 as a percentage of the maximum 125

solution_steps.action: add the five subject marks of the row
solution_steps.compute: test_total = sum((maths_mark, science_mark, sst_mark, hindi_mark, eng_mark))

solution_steps.explain: 102 out of a possible 125 gives 102 * 100 / 125 = 81.6 percent

concepts.title: Median of Even Unit Test Column
concepts.definition: DataFrame median() returns the middle of an ordered column. With an even count of values there is no single middle entry, so the median becomes the average of the two central values; for the four Maths marks of Unit Test 1, ordered as 15, 20, 22, 23, the middle pair 20 and 22 averages to 21.
concepts.key_idea: Sort the column, take the two central values of an even-sized batch and average them.
question_patterns: find the median of the Maths marks in UT1 for values 22, 20, 23 and 15

solution_steps.explain: the ordered UT1 Maths marks 15, 20, 22, 23 carry the middle pair 20 and 22
(20 + 22) / 2 = 21.0, the median printed by the program

concepts.title: Mode of the Hindi Column
concepts.definition: The mode is the entry that shows up most often in a column. In the Hindi column of marksUT the value 24 appears three times, more than any other mark, so mode() returns 24; the frequency of the mode against the total number of entries measures how dominant it is.
concepts.key_idea: Count each value's occurrences, keep the largest count, and divide it by the column size for the mode's share.

solution_steps.explain: 24 occurs 3 times against 2 for both 25 and 22, so max of the counts is 3

concepts.title: GROUP BY UT-wise Mean
concepts.definition: GROUP BY splits a DataFrame into buckets sharing a key value, applies an aggregate to each bucket and combines the results (the split-apply-combine strategy). Grouping the marksUT data by UT and averaging Maths gives 20.00, 21.50 and 16.25 for the three tests, each a plain total divided by the group size.
concepts.key_idea: Sum the marks inside one group, divide by how many rows the group holds; agg('mean') does this per bucket.
question_patterns: find the average Maths marks of all students in Unit Test 3 using GROUP BY
compute the mean of the UT3 Maths marks 14, 22, 12 and 17

solution_steps.action: total the marks inside one group
solution_steps.explain: the UT3 bucket of Maths holds 14 + 22 + 12 + 17 = 65
65 shared by the 4 students of the group gives 16.25, matching the chapter output

worked_examples.q: Which three-word strategy names GROUP BY's working: split, apply and combine?

concepts.title: pivot_table Mean for Duplicate Entries
concepts.definition: pivot() refuses data whose index columns repeat, but pivot_table() accepts duplicates by aggregating them, with mean as the default aggregate. Two blue-pen rows priced 50 and 20 collapse into one pivot cell holding their mean 35, and any aggregate such as sum, max or len can be named through aggfunc instead.
concepts.key_idea: Duplicate pivot keys are merged by averaging; the cell value is the group's total divided by its row count.
question_patterns: what price does pivot_table report for the blue pen whose rows cost 50 and 20

solution_steps.explain: the two blue-pen prices 50 and 20 add to 70
70 divided by the 2 rows gives the pivot cell 35.0 shown in the chapter

concepts.title: fillna Percentage for Missing Marks
concepts.definition: Missing marks stored as NaN can be filled before computing a result: fillna(0) substitutes zero, fillna(method='pad') copies the previous value, and the chosen estimate changes the percentage. Filling Raman's absent Science mark of Unit Test 4 with zero gives the filled total 60 over the full ceiling of 100, that is 60 percent.
concepts.key_idea: Fill the gaps first, then total and scale; every estimate changes the percentage, so the choice must be stated.
concepts.textbook_ref: leip103.txt sections 3.8.1-3.8.3, Program 3-12 and fillna code (lines 1555-1878)
question_patterns: after fillna(0) on Raman's Science marks 21, 20, 19 and a missing fourth test, compute the percentage

solution_steps.explain: 21 + 20 + 19 plus the filled 0 gives 60
60 out of 4 tests of 25 marks each gives 60 * 100 / 100 = 60 percent

worked_examples.q: Filling an absent mark with zero gives a filled total of 60 over a ceiling of 100. What percentage is that?

concepts.title: Sorting Values and Altering the Index
concepts.definition: sort_values(by, axis, ascending) orders the rows of a DataFrame by one or more columns, with later columns breaking ties, and ascending=False flipping the direction. reset_index() rebuilds a clean continuous index after a slice while keeping or dropping the old one, and set_index() promotes any column to be the row index.
concepts.key_idea: First column sorts, extra columns break ties; reset_index renumbers, set_index relabels by a data column.
question_patterns: write the statement to sort the marksUT data by the Name column in ascending order

solution_steps.explain: by lists the columns; the first decides the order and the rest break ties
ascending=True is the default; ascending=False reverses it
reset_index rebuilds 0, 1, 2...; set_index promotes a chosen column to the index

worked_examples.q: Which argument flips sort_values() to descending order?

concepts.title: MySQL Import Export with sqlalchemy
concepts.definition: A pandas DataFrame exchanges data with MySQL through a connection engine: sqlalchemy's create_engine() takes a connection string of driver, username, password, host, port and database; read_sql_query(), read_sql_table() and read_sql() pull data into a DataFrame, and to_sql() writes it back with if_exists choosing fail, replace or append.
concepts.key_idea: Build the engine once from the connection string; read functions import, to_sql exports, and if_exists controls clashes.
question_patterns: which two libraries must be installed to link pandas with MySQL

solution_steps.explain: create_engine('mysql+pymysql://user:password@host:3306/database') returns the engine
read_sql_query fetches query results; read_sql_table fetches a whole table; read_sql accepts either
to_sql writes the DataFrame, and if_exists decides between fail, replace and append
